stories.title: Let There Be Light

verses.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.

levels.tip: Tap the letters in order, then ✓. Or slide your finger across them.
Real words that aren’t in the verse are bonus words. Each one earns a drop of lamp oil.
Stuck? A hint reveals one letter and costs 1 oil.
From memory: tap the words in the right order.

stories.note: The Bible opens with God speaking light into darkness. Light is the first thing named in creation, and the same theme returns at the very end of Revelation.
stories.draw: EXISTING Picture A — vast dark ocean, golden light breaking through swirling clouds

stories.title: A Garden Eastward in Eden

verses.text: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

levels.tip: From memory: tap the words in the right order.

stories.note: Every person is made in the image of God. That is the root of human dignity, and it is stated before anything else is said about us.
stories.draw: a lush garden at sunrise, a river winding between fruit trees, mist over green meadows, no people

stories.title: Where Art Thou?

verses.text: And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?
And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

levels.tip: From memory: tap the words in the right order.

stories.note: After the first sin, God comes looking for man. Genesis 3:15 is often called the first gospel: the promise of a seed of the woman who would crush the serpent.
stories.draw: a single fruit tree at twilight in the garden, a serpent coiled on a low branch, the garden gate glowing far behind

stories.title: A Token of a Covenant

verses.text: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.
And the LORD said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.

stories.note: The rainbow is God's own sign that he will never again destroy the earth by flood. It is the first covenant named in the Bible, and it is made with every living creature.
stories.draw: the wooden ark resting on a mountain top after the flood, a rainbow arching across a clearing sky, still water below

stories.title: Get Thee Out of Thy Country

verses.text: Now the LORD had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee:
And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:
And he believed in the LORD; and he counted it to him for righteousness.

stories.note: Abram left everything on God's word alone. Genesis 15:6 is quoted three times in the New Testament (Romans 4:3, Galatians 3:6, James 2:23) to show that righteousness comes by faith.
stories.draw: a desert caravan of camels and tents setting out at dawn across wide plains, seen from far behind, stars fading above

stories.title: Is Any Thing Too Hard?

verses.text: Is any thing too hard for the LORD? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.
And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.

stories.note: Sarah was ninety when Isaac was born. His name means "he laughs", and the promise came true at exactly the time appointed.
stories.draw: tents beneath great oak trees at Mamre in the evening, a cooking fire, three travellers seen only as distant silhouettes on the path

stories.title: God Will Provide

verses.text: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.
And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.

stories.note: Jehovahjireh means "the LORD will see to it" or "the LORD will provide." A substitute died in the son's place, a picture the New Testament sees fulfilled in Christ.
stories.draw: a lone mountain top at first light, a ram caught by its horns in a thicket beside a stone altar, no people

stories.title: Surely the LORD Is in This Place

verses.text: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.

And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.
And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not.

stories.note: Jacob was running away when God met him. He named the place Bethel, "house of God." Jesus refers to this ladder in John 1:51.
stories.draw: a rocky hillside at night, a stone used as a pillow, a stairway of golden light rising into a starry sky

stories.title: God Meant It unto Good

verses.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.
But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

stories.note: Joseph was sold by his brothers, falsely accused and forgotten in prison, yet God used every step to save his family. This is one of the clearest pictures of providence in Scripture.
stories.draw: a richly coloured coat lying on a rock in the desert, and far away the granaries of Egypt along the Nile at sunset

stories.title: Holy Ground

verses.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.
And he said, Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.

stories.note: Here God reveals his name, I AM. Jesus takes up the same words in John 8:58, "Before Abraham was, I am."
stories.draw: a desert bush burning with bright golden fire that does not consume it, on a mountainside, a pair of sandals left on the ground

stories.title: Let My People Go

verses.text: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.

And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

stories.note: The Passover lamb's blood marked the houses God would pass over. Paul writes, "Christ our passover is sacrificed for us" (1 Corinthians 5:7).
stories.draw: an Egyptian village street at night, one doorway glowing with lamplight, a red mark on its doorposts, a full moon over the palms

stories.title: The LORD Shall Fight for You

verses.text: And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.
The LORD shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.
And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

stories.note: Trapped between the sea and Pharaoh's army, Israel was told to stand still. The deliverance at the Red Sea is remembered throughout the Psalms and the prophets.
stories.draw: towering walls of sea water parted on either side of a dry path, a pillar of fire glowing behind, night turning to dawn

stories.title: The Ten Commandments

verses.text: I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

stories.note: The commandments begin with what God had already done: he brought them out of slavery. The law was given to a people already redeemed. Paul calls the fifth "the first commandment with promise" (Ephesians 6:2).
stories.draw: Mount Sinai wrapped in dark storm clouds and lightning, two blank stone tablets resting on a rock in the foreground

stories.title: Love Thy Neighbour

verses.text: Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy: for I the LORD your God am holy.
Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the LORD.

stories.note: Jesus called this the second great commandment (Matthew 22:39). It sits in Leviticus beside the law to leave the corners of the field for the poor (19:9-10).
stories.draw: a wheat field at harvest with the corners left uncut, sheaves stacked, a village on a hill in warm evening light

stories.title: The Feasts of the LORD

verses.text: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of the LORD, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.
These are the feasts of the LORD, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.
In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the LORD's passover.

stories.note: The Hebrew word for feasts, moedim, means "appointed times." Leviticus 23 sets out God's calendar, from Passover in spring to Tabernacles in autumn.
stories.draw: a full moon rising over Jerusalem's hills in spring, lamps lit in courtyards, a table set with unleavened bread

stories.title: The LORD Bless Thee

verses.text: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee:
The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee:
The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.

stories.note: This is the priestly blessing Aaron spoke over Israel. Silver scrolls with these words, from about 600 BC, were found at Ketef Hinnom in Jerusalem. They are among the oldest Bible texts known.
stories.draw: the sun rising over a camp of tents in the wilderness, soft golden light spreading across the sand, smoke rising from cook fires

stories.title: A Star out of Jacob

verses.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.
God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?

I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.

stories.note: Jesus applied the bronze serpent to himself in John 3:14. Balaam was hired to curse Israel but could only bless, and he foresaw a Star and a Sceptre coming out of Jacob.
stories.draw: a bronze serpent on a tall pole above a desert camp at dusk, a single bright star rising over the far hills

stories.title: Hear, O Israel

verses.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD:
And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:

stories.note: The Shema is still prayed by Jewish people every morning and evening. Jesus named it the first and greatest commandment (Mark 12:29-30).
stories.draw: the wooden doorpost of a stone house with a small case fixed to it, morning light, the hills of Canaan beyond

stories.title: Choose Life

verses.text: The secret things belong unto the LORD our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.
I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:

stories.note: At the end of his life Moses set two ways before the people. God's revealed word is given so that it can be lived, not just studied.
stories.draw: a lone figure seen from behind on the top of Mount Nebo, looking out over the Jordan valley and the promised land in golden haze

stories.title: He Will Not Fail Thee

verses.text: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
And the LORD, he it is that doth go before thee; he will be with thee, he will not fail thee, neither forsake thee: fear not, neither be dismayed.

stories.note: Moses spoke these words as he handed leadership to Joshua. Hebrews 13:5 quotes the promise: "I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee."
stories.draw: a river crossing at dawn, the Jordan flowing between reeds, the promised land green on the far side, a column of people seen from far behind

stories.title: Be Strong and of a Good Courage

verses.text: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

stories.note: Joshua's success was tied to meditating on God's word day and night. The command to be strong comes three times in this one chapter.
stories.draw: an open scroll on a stone beside a riverbank camp at dawn, spears and tents in soft focus, the walls of Jericho far off

stories.title: Choose You This Day

verses.text: And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.
And the people said unto Joshua, The LORD our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey.

stories.note: Joshua set up a great stone under the oak as a witness to this promise (24:26). "As for me and my house" is still painted over many front doors.
stories.draw: a great oak tree beside a large standing stone at Shechem, hills all around, evening light

stories.title: Thou Mighty Man of Valour

verses.text: And the angel of the LORD appeared unto him, and said unto him, The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.
And the LORD looked upon him, and said, Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?
In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

stories.note: Gideon was hiding when God called him a mighty man of valour. The book of Judges ends in disorder because everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
stories.draw: a stone winepress hidden among rocks, a fleece of wool on the threshing floor wet with dew, early morning

stories.title: Whither Thou Goest

verses.text: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God:
The LORD recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the LORD God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.

stories.note: Ruth was a Moabite widow who chose Israel's God. She became the great-grandmother of King David and is named in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1:5).
stories.draw: a golden barley field at harvest near Bethlehem, a young woman gleaning seen from behind, sheaves left along the edge

stories.title: Speak; for Thy Servant Heareth

verses.text: For this child I prayed; and the LORD hath given me my petition which I asked of him:
And ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was, and Samuel was laid down to sleep;
And the LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.

stories.note: Samuel was the answer to his mother Hannah's prayer. God called him by name while the lamp of God was still burning.
stories.draw: the inside of the tabernacle at night, a golden lampstand burning low, a sleeping mat on the floor, deep shadows

stories.title: The Battle Is the LORD's

verses.text: But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD's, and he will give you into our hands.

stories.note: God chose the youngest son, the one his family overlooked. David fought in the name of the LORD, not with Saul's armour.
stories.draw: the valley of Elah, a clear brook with five smooth stones in the water and a shepherd's sling on the bank, armies as tiny tents on two hills

stories.title: The LORD Is My Rock

verses.text: And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
And he said, The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;
As for God, his way is perfect; the word of the LORD is tried: he is a buckler to all them that trust in him.

stories.note: God promised David a throne established for ever. The New Testament opens by calling Jesus "the son of David" (Matthew 1:1).
stories.draw: a rocky mountain stronghold at sunset, cliffs and caves like the wilderness of En Gedi, a harp resting on a stone ledge

stories.title: An Understanding Heart

verses.text: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?
And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea shore.
But will God indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?

stories.note: Solomon could have asked for anything and asked for wisdom. At the temple's dedication he confessed that no building could contain God.
stories.draw: Solomon's temple in Jerusalem at dawn, golden light on stone and cedar, smoke rising from the altar court

stories.title: A Still Small Voice

verses.text: And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.
And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces: and they said, The LORD, he is the God; the LORD, he is the God.
And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.

stories.note: After the fire fell on Carmel, Elijah fled in fear. God spoke to him not in wind, earthquake or fire, but in a still small voice.
stories.draw: fire falling from a dark sky onto a stone altar on Mount Carmel, water in the trench around it turning to steam, the sea far below

stories.title: They That Be with Us

verses.text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.

And Elisha prayed, and said, LORD, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.

stories.note: Elisha's servant saw only the enemy army until God opened his eyes. Hebrews 1:14 describes angels as ministering spirits sent for those who will inherit salvation.
stories.draw: hills around a small walled town at night, ringed by horses and chariots of fire glowing in the darkness, no riders' faces

stories.title: Thine Is the Greatness

verses.text: O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.

Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and thou art exalted as head above all.

stories.note: David sang this when the ark came to Jerusalem. His prayer in 29:11 echoes in the closing words of the Lord's Prayer, "thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory."
stories.draw: the ark of the covenant carried in procession up to Jerusalem, golden cymbals and harps catching the light, people seen only from behind

stories.title: Heal Their Land

verses.text: If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.

stories.note: God gave this promise to Solomon after the temple was dedicated. The order is humble, pray, seek and turn; then God hears, forgives and heals.
stories.draw: green fields and terraced hills after a long drought, rain clouds parting, sunlight on wet earth, the temple far away on its hill

stories.title: Prepared His Heart

verses.text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.

And they sang together by course in praising and giving thanks unto the LORD; because he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever toward Israel. And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid.

stories.note: Ezra's order is a pattern for every Bible teacher: seek the word, do it, then teach it.
stories.draw: an open scroll on a stone table beside an oil lamp, the foundations of the rebuilt temple behind in morning light

stories.title: The Joy of the LORD

verses.text: Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength.
So the wall was finished in the twenty and fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty and two days.

stories.note: The wall went up in fifty-two days despite open opposition. When the law was read and the people wept, they were told that the joy of the LORD was their strength.
stories.draw: the rebuilt walls and gates of Jerusalem at sunrise, scaffolding just removed, stones fresh and golden

stories.title: For Such a Time as This

verses.text: For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father's house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?

Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.

stories.note: God's name never appears in Esther, yet his hand is on every page. The deliverance is still remembered every year at Purim.
stories.draw: a Persian palace hall with tall columns and hanging lamps, a golden sceptre held out from an empty throne, rich curtains

stories.title: I Know That My Redeemer Liveth

verses.text: And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.

stories.note: In his deepest loss Job still looked for a living Redeemer. God answered him from the whirlwind, not with an explanation but by showing his own greatness.
stories.draw: a vast night sky full of stars over a lonely desert plain, the first glow of morning on the horizon

stories.title: Like a Tree Planted

verses.text: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.
But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.
And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

stories.note: The whole book of Psalms opens with meditating on God's word. Jeremiah 17:7-8 uses the same picture of a tree by the water.
stories.draw: a great green tree planted by a clear river, heavy with fruit, its leaves shining in late afternoon light

stories.title: The Heavens Declare

verses.text: When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained;
What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him?
The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork.

stories.note: David, a shepherd under the open sky, saw the stars as a message about their Maker. Paul makes the same point in Romans 1:20.
stories.draw: the Milky Way arching over dark hills, a crescent moon, a shepherd's fire small in the valley below

stories.title: The LORD Is My Shepherd

verses.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake.

stories.note: David, once a shepherd himself, wrote of God as his shepherd. Jesus said, "I am the good shepherd" (John 10:11).
stories.draw: green pastures beside still water in a quiet valley, a flock of sheep grazing, a shepherd's staff leaning on a rock

stories.title: Goodness and Mercy

verses.text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.
Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

stories.note: In the valley the psalm changes from "he" to "thou." God is no longer only talked about; he is talked to. The psalm ends at home in God's house.
stories.draw: a narrow path through a deep shadowed valley opening onto a lit house and table in the distance, a lamp in the window

stories.title: God Is Our Refuge

verses.text: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.

stories.note: Psalm 46 inspired Martin Luther's hymn "A Mighty Fortress Is Our God." "Be still" here means stop striving and know who is God.
stories.draw: a stone fortress on a high rock above a stormy sea, waves breaking far below, calm light within its gate

stories.title: Create in Me a Clean Heart

verses.text: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

stories.note: David wrote Psalm 51 after Nathan confronted him over his sin with Bathsheba. The word "create" is the same Hebrew word used in Genesis 1:1, because only God can make a new heart.
stories.draw: fresh snow on a quiet hillside at dawn, a clear stream running through it, a sprig of hyssop on a stone

stories.title: Teach Us to Number Our Days

verses.text: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.
For a thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.
So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.

stories.note: Psalm 90 is titled "A Prayer of Moses," which makes it probably the oldest psalm. Peter echoes verse 4 in 2 Peter 3:8: one day is with the Lord as a thousand years.
stories.draw: ancient mountains under a sky of slowly turning stars, an hourglass on a rock in the foreground, dawn on the horizon

stories.title: Under His Wings

verses.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.

stories.note: The psalm promises shelter to the one who dwells, not just visits. Satan quoted verse 11 to tempt Jesus (Matthew 4:6), and Jesus answered with Scripture.
stories.draw: a great eagle with outspread wings sheltering its young on a high cliff nest, storm clouds parting behind

stories.title: Bless the LORD, O My Soul

verses.text: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.

stories.note: East and west never meet. That is how far God removes forgiven sin. Psalm 103 then reminds us to "forget not all his benefits."
stories.draw: the gates of a city at sunrise with crowds entering, seen from behind, banners and palm branches, light flooding through the arch

stories.title: This Is the Day

verses.text: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.
This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.

stories.note: Jesus applied Psalm 118:22 to himself (Matthew 21:42), and Peter preached it (Acts 4:11). The Psalms end with every breathing thing called to praise.
stories.draw: a single great cornerstone set at the corner of a new stone building, sunrise light, a builder's discarded rubble pile nearby

stories.title: A Lamp unto My Feet

verses.text: Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.
Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.

stories.note: Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible: 176 verses, arranged in 22 sections, one for each letter of the Hebrew alphabet, all about God's word. This game takes its name from verse 105.
stories.draw: EXISTING Picture B — an oil lamp lighting a dark path at night (optional redo in Picture A style)

stories.title: I Will Lift Up Mine Eyes

verses.text: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth.
The LORD shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.

stories.note: This is one of the Songs of Degrees, sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the feasts. Help comes not from the hills, but from the Maker of the hills.
stories.draw: a traveller's path winding up through rolling hills toward Jerusalem, seen from behind, morning mist in the valleys

stories.title: Fearfully and Wonderfully Made

verses.text: Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?
I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:

stories.note: There is nowhere God is not present, not even "the uttermost parts of the sea" (139:9). He knew each of us before we were born.
stories.draw: dawn breaking over the sea at the far edge of the world, light reaching into every shadow of the waves

stories.title: The Beginning of Knowledge

verses.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

stories.note: Proverbs begins where all wisdom begins, with the fear of the LORD. Then it turns to practical life: the heart and the tongue.
stories.draw: a quiet study with an open scroll, an oil lamp and a window looking out on a garden spring

stories.title: Trust in the LORD

verses.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

stories.note: "Lean not" pictures resting your whole weight on something. The promise is that God will make your paths straight.
stories.draw: a stony path winding straight up through a wide valley to a lit city on a hill, the way made clear by evening light

stories.title: A Strong Tower

verses.text: A man's heart deviseth his way: but the LORD directeth his steps.
The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

stories.note: We make our plans, but the LORD directs our steps. In trouble the righteous run to his name, which means to his character.
stories.draw: a tall stone watchtower in a vineyard on a hillside at dusk, light in its window, a path leading up to the door

stories.title: A Time to Every Purpose

verses.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
He hath made every thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

stories.note: The Preacher searched for meaning "under the sun" and found everything empty without God. His conclusion is that God has made everything beautiful in its time.
stories.draw: one great tree shown through the seasons, blossoms on one side and autumn gold on the other, under a wide sky

stories.title: The Winter Is Past

verses.text: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;
The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.

stories.note: The Song celebrates love between bride and groom as a gift from God. The "turtle" is the turtledove, whose call marked the coming of spring.
stories.draw: a vineyard in spring, blossoms on the vines and almond trees, turtle doves on a stone wall, soft rain clouds moving away

stories.title: Come Now, and Let Us Reason

verses.text: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

stories.note: God invites guilty people to reason with him, and offers cleansing. Isaiah 2:4 looks ahead to a kingdom of peace; its words are carved on a wall across from the United Nations in New York.
stories.draw: fresh white wool and fresh snow beside a scarlet cloth on a stone, in clear morning light, a ploughshare leaning nearby

stories.title: Here Am I; Send Me

verses.text: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.
Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.

stories.note: Isaiah saw the LORD's holiness and his own sin, was cleansed, and then volunteered. John 12:41 says Isaiah saw Christ's glory.
stories.draw: a vast temple filled with smoke and golden light, a high throne only suggested by brightness, a burning coal on an altar

stories.title: Unto Us a Child Is Born

verses.text: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.

For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.

stories.note: Immanuel means "God with us" (Matthew 1:23). These prophecies were written about 700 years before Jesus was born.
stories.draw: a great light dawning over dark hills of Galilee, villages still in shadow, the first rays reaching the valleys

stories.title: The Word of Our God Shall Stand

verses.text: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God.
The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.

stories.note: All four Gospels apply 40:3 to John the Baptist. Grass and flowers fade, but God's word lasts for ever (1 Peter 1:24-25).
stories.draw: a desert highway straightened through the wilderness, wild grass and flowers withering at its edge, a clear dawn ahead

stories.title: Wings as Eagles

verses.text: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.

stories.note: To "wait upon the LORD" is to hope in him with expectation. Strength is exchanged, not earned.
stories.draw: an eagle soaring high above mountain peaks at sunrise, wings spread on the wind, clouds far below

stories.title: My Counsel Shall Stand

verses.text: Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure:
For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD.
So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it.

stories.note: Only God declares the end from the beginning. Like rain that waters the earth (55:10), his word always does what he sends it to do.
stories.draw: rain falling on a wide landscape and rising again as mist, crops springing up, a distant mountain under the open sky

stories.title: Wounded for Our Transgressions

verses.text: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.

stories.note: Isaiah 53 describes the suffering servant in detail. In Acts 8:35 Philip began at this passage and preached Jesus. A complete copy of Isaiah was found among the Dead Sea Scrolls.
stories.draw: a flock of sheep scattered across rocky hills at dusk, one lamb standing alone in a pool of light

stories.title: Arise, Shine

verses.text: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee.

The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;

stories.note: Jesus read Isaiah 61:1 in the synagogue at Nazareth and said, "This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears" (Luke 4:21).
stories.draw: Jerusalem's walls lit by a great golden sunrise, light pouring over the city while the surrounding land is still dark

stories.title: Before I Formed Thee

verses.text: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.
O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the LORD. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel.

stories.note: God knew Jeremiah before he was born and called him to speak to the nations. At the potter's house he learned that God can reshape a marred vessel.
stories.draw: a potter's workshop, a clay vessel turning on the wheel, finished jars on shelves, warm light through the doorway

stories.title: Thoughts of Peace

verses.text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart.
Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not.

stories.note: This promise was sent to exiles in Babylon, with a set time of seventy years (29:10). Daniel read this very letter in Daniel 9:2.
stories.draw: a family's lamp-lit home in Babylon by a river, willow trees, and a road leading west toward a far-off dawn

stories.title: New Every Morning

verses.text: It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.
They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.

stories.note: Written over the ruins of Jerusalem, Lamentations has hope at its exact centre. The hymn "Great Is Thy Faithfulness" comes from verse 23.
stories.draw: the ruins of a city at first light, new grass growing between fallen stones, a bright sunrise breaking through

stories.title: Can These Bones Live?

verses.text: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.
And he said unto me, Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord GOD, thou knowest.
Again he said unto me, Prophesy upon these bones, and say unto them, O ye dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.

stories.note: God promised a new heart and new life for a people who seemed dead. Ezekiel 37 pictures the nation of Israel being brought back to life by God's word and Spirit.
stories.draw: a wide valley at dawn with pale scattered stones and old bones half hidden in grass, a strong wind sweeping through and light breaking over the hills

stories.title: Daniel Purposed in His Heart

verses.text: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
Daniel answered and said, Blessed be the name of God for ever and ever: for wisdom and might are his:
And he changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise, and knowledge to them that know understanding:

stories.note: Daniel decided ahead of time, as a teenager far from home. When God revealed the king's dream to him, his first response was praise.
stories.draw: a simple meal of vegetables and water on a table in a Babylonian palace room, a window looking toward the west

stories.title: A Kingdom Never Destroyed

verses.text: He revealeth the deep and secret things: he knoweth what is in the darkness, and the light dwelleth with him.

And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.

stories.note: Nebuchadnezzar's image showed a series of kingdoms from Babylon onward. The stone cut out without hands becomes a mountain that fills the whole earth (2:35).
stories.draw: a colossal statue of gold, silver, bronze and iron standing on a plain, a stone cut from a distant mountain flying toward its feet

stories.title: But If Not

verses.text: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king.
But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of God.

stories.note: Their faith did not depend on being rescued: "but if not." They went into the fire, and they were not alone in it.
stories.draw: a blazing furnace in the plain of Dura at night, four figures seen only as dark silhouettes walking calmly in the flames

stories.title: Weighed in the Balances

verses.text: And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.

stories.note: Belshazzar drank from the temple vessels and that same night Babylon fell to the Medes and Persians (5:30). Secular records confirm Belshazzar was co-regent with his father Nabonidus.
stories.draw: a vast Babylonian banquet hall lit by lamps, golden cups on long tables, a strange bright glow on the plaster wall opposite the lampstand, no writing

stories.title: The Lions' Den

verses.text: Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

stories.note: Daniel kept praying "as he did aforetime," even when it became illegal. He was well over eighty years old.
stories.draw: an open window in an upper room facing toward Jerusalem at evening, and below, a stone den where lions lie peacefully in a shaft of light

stories.title: They That Be Wise Shall Shine

verses.text: Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.
And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.

stories.note: The seventy weeks prophecy came to Daniel while he was praying over Jeremiah's seventy years. Daniel's book ends with the promise that the wise will shine like the stars.
stories.draw: a night sky blazing with stars over the river Tigris, a scroll open on the bank in the starlight

stories.title: As the Morning

verses.text: Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the LORD: his going forth is prepared as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.
For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.

stories.note: Jesus quoted Hosea 6:6 twice (Matthew 9:13; 12:7). God wants hearts that know him, not ritual alone.
stories.draw: soft spring rain falling on ploughed fields at sunrise, puddles catching the gold light, a farmhouse in the distance

stories.title: I Will Pour Out My Spirit

verses.text: And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.
And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions:

stories.note: Peter quoted Joel 2:28 on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2:16-17). God promises to restore even the years that were lost.
stories.draw: green fields restored after a locust plague, new crops rising, a bright sky with rays pouring down over the land

stories.title: Let Judgment Run Down as Waters

verses.text: Surely the Lord GOD will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.
But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

stories.note: Amos was a herdsman and a gatherer of sycamore fruit, not a professional prophet. Dr Martin Luther King Jr quoted 5:24 in his "I Have a Dream" speech.
stories.draw: a mighty stream rushing down from mountains through a dry valley, fig trees and sheepfolds along its banks

stories.title: The Kingdom Shall Be the LORD's

verses.text: For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.
And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the LORD's.

stories.note: Obadiah is the shortest book of the Old Testament, one chapter of 21 verses. Edom trusted its cliffs, but the kingdom belongs to the LORD.
stories.draw: red rock cliffs of Edom with city dwellings carved into the stone, and far across the valley Mount Zion in morning light

stories.title: Salvation Is of the LORD

verses.text: Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah. And Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.

stories.note: Jesus pointed to Jonah's three days and three nights as the sign of his own death and resurrection (Matthew 12:40).
stories.draw: a stormy sea at night with a small wooden ship above, and beneath the waves the dark shape of a great fish

stories.title: Walk Humbly with Thy God

verses.text: But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

stories.note: Micah named Bethlehem as the Messiah's birthplace about 700 years ahead; the chief priests quoted it to Herod (Matthew 2:5-6). Micah 6:8 sums up what God requires.
stories.draw: the small town of Bethlehem on its hill at night, terraced olive groves, a single bright star overhead

stories.title: A Strong Hold in the Day of Trouble

verses.text: The LORD is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: the LORD hath his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.

stories.note: Nahum foretold the fall of Nineveh, which happened in 612 BC. The same God who judges the proud is a stronghold to those who trust him.
stories.draw: a mountain fortress standing firm above a whirlwind storm, clouds of dust rolling over the plain below

stories.title: The Just Shall Live by His Faith

verses.text: For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but the just shall live by his faith.
Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation.

stories.note: "The just shall live by his faith" is quoted three times in the New Testament (Romans 1:17, Galatians 3:11, Hebrews 10:38). Habakkuk chose joy even with no figs, no fruit and no flock.
stories.draw: a watchtower on a city wall at dawn, a clay tablet propped against the parapet, a barren fig tree below and the sun rising

stories.title: He Will Rejoice over Thee

verses.text: For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD, to serve him with one consent.
The LORD thy God in the midst of thee is mighty; he will save, he will rejoice over thee with joy; he will rest in his love, he will joy over thee with singing.

stories.note: Most of Zephaniah warns of the day of the LORD, but it ends with God himself singing over his people.
stories.draw: Jerusalem at dawn with lamps still burning in the windows, a gentle golden light over the whole city, birds rising

stories.title: Consider Your Ways

verses.text: Now therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways.
The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith the LORD of hosts: and in this place will I give peace, saith the LORD of hosts.

stories.note: Haggai's four messages are each dated to the day in 520 BC. The latter house was greater because the Messiah himself would walk in it.
stories.draw: the half-built second temple in Jerusalem, stone foundations and scaffolding, a bright sky promising rain

stories.title: Not by Might, nor by Power

verses.text: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.

Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.
And the LORD shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one LORD, and his name one.

stories.note: Zechariah 9:9 was fulfilled when Jesus rode into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:5). Chapter 14 looks ahead to the day the LORD is king over all the earth.
stories.draw: a golden lampstand between two olive trees, oil flowing to its lamps, set on a hillside facing the Mount of Olives at dawn

stories.title: The Sun of Righteousness

verses.text: For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.
But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.

stories.note: Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament. After it, about four hundred years passed before the next prophet, John the Baptist, appeared.
stories.draw: the sun rising over fields with calves running free from their stall, warm light streaming across the grass

stories.title: We Have Seen His Star

verses.text: Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.

And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.

stories.note: The wise men came from the east, perhaps Babylon or Persia, where Daniel had once served. They found the child in a house, not the stable, possibly up to two years later (2:16).
stories.draw: a bright star over the hills of Bethlehem at night, camels and travellers seen as distant silhouettes on the road below

stories.title: Follow Me

verses.text: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

stories.note: Jesus answered each temptation with "It is written," quoting Deuteronomy each time. Then he called ordinary fishermen to follow him.
stories.draw: fishing boats pulled up on the shore of the Sea of Galilee at dawn, nets drying on the rocks, mist on the water

stories.title: The Beatitudes

verses.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

stories.note: The Sermon on the Mount opens with eight blessings that turn the world's values upside down. It begins with the poor in spirit, those who know they need God.
stories.draw: a grassy hillside above the Sea of Galilee in soft afternoon light, wildflowers, a crowd seated far off seen from behind

stories.title: The Light of the World

verses.text: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.
Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.
Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.

stories.note: Jesus said, "I am the light of the world" (John 8:12), and told his followers that they are too. A lamp is lit to be seen.
stories.draw: a city of white stone set on a hill at night, its windows glowing, and in the foreground an oil lamp on a stand inside a doorway

stories.title: The Lord's Prayer

verses.text: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread.
And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

stories.note: Jesus gave this prayer as a pattern: "After this manner." It puts God's name, kingdom and will first, and then our daily needs.
stories.draw: a quiet olive grove at first light, a simple room's open window looking out on it, a loaf of bread on the sill

stories.title: Seek Ye First

verses.text: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you:

stories.note: Worry looks at tomorrow; faith looks at the Father who feeds the birds. Put his kingdom first and he takes care of the rest.
stories.draw: birds flying over a field of wild lilies in bloom, a barn far off, warm afternoon light

stories.title: Come unto Me

verses.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

stories.note: A yoke joined two animals to pull together. Jesus offers to share the load, and calls his yoke "easy," meaning well-fitting.
stories.draw: a wooden yoke resting on a stone wall beside a quiet field at sunset, oxen grazing freely nearby

stories.title: Be of Good Cheer

verses.text: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus.
And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?

stories.note: Peter walked on water while he looked at Jesus and began to sink when he looked at the wind. Even then, Jesus caught him immediately.
stories.draw: a fishing boat tossed on a stormy lake at night, and far across the waves a single figure walking on the water, seen only as a silhouette in moonlight

stories.title: My Words Shall Not Pass Away

verses.text: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.
Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.
But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.

stories.note: On the Mount of Olives Jesus told his disciples about the signs before his return. He said to learn the lesson of the fig tree and to watch, because no one knows the day or the hour.
stories.draw: a fig tree putting out new leaves on the Mount of Olives at dusk, the temple mount across the valley, storm light on the horizon

stories.title: Go Ye Therefore

verses.text: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.

stories.note: The risen Christ sent his followers to all nations with a promise: "I am with you alway." Matthew's Gospel ends with that promise.
stories.draw: an empty garden tomb at sunrise with the great stone rolled away, linen cloths folded inside, lilies by the path

stories.title: Behold, a Sower

verses.text: Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow:
And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.

stories.note: Jesus explained this parable himself: the seed is the word. The same seed fell on every kind of ground; the difference was the soil.
stories.draw: a field being sown at morning, seed scattered over a path, rocks, thorns and good dark soil, birds overhead

stories.title: Peace, Be Still

verses.text: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

stories.note: Only God rules the sea (Psalm 89:9). The disciples' question, "What manner of man is this?", is the question of Mark's whole Gospel.
stories.draw: the Sea of Galilee suddenly calm after a storm, clouds breaking, moonlight on glassy water, a small boat resting

stories.title: All Things Are Possible

verses.text: Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.
And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
And Jesus looking upon them saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.

stories.note: The father's honest prayer, "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief," was enough. Jesus healed his son.
stories.draw: a narrow mountain pass opening onto a bright valley, the path ahead lit through the gap in the rocks

stories.title: With God Nothing Shall Be Impossible

verses.text: For with God nothing shall be impossible.
And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her.
And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord,
And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.

stories.note: Mary answered the impossible with trust: "be it unto me according to thy word." Her song, the Magnificat, is full of echoes of Hannah's prayer in 1 Samuel 2.
stories.draw: a simple stone house in Nazareth at dawn, a lily in a clay jar on the windowsill, light streaming into the room

stories.title: Good Tidings of Great Joy

verses.text: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.

stories.note: The first announcement of Christ's birth went to shepherds in the fields near Bethlehem, the city of David the shepherd king.
stories.draw: shepherds' fields outside Bethlehem at night, sheep resting, the sky opening with soft golden light, the town small on the hill

stories.title: Go, and Do Thou Likewise

verses.text: And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.
But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him,
And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

stories.note: A lawyer asked, "Who is my neighbour?" Jesus turned the question around: the neighbour was the one who showed mercy, and he was a Samaritan.
stories.draw: the steep rocky road from Jerusalem down to Jericho in late afternoon, a donkey tied outside a lit roadside inn

stories.title: Lost and Found

verses.text: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?
And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.

stories.note: Luke 15 has three parables of lost things: a sheep, a coin and a son. Each ends in rejoicing, and the father ran to meet his son.
stories.draw: a shepherd seen from behind carrying a lamb on his shoulders down a hillside at dusk, a village lamp glowing below

stories.title: Remember Me

verses.text: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.
And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

stories.note: Even on the cross Jesus prayed for those who crucified him. A dying thief asked to be remembered and was promised paradise that same day.
stories.draw: three empty crosses on a distant hill under a darkened sky, a thin line of light breaking on the horizon

stories.title: Did Not Our Heart Burn?

verses.text: And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.
And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

stories.note: The risen Jesus taught from Moses and all the prophets about himself. The whole Old Testament points to him.
stories.draw: a dusty road at sunset winding toward a small village, three travellers seen from far behind, a lamp lit in a doorway ahead

stories.title: In the Beginning Was the Word

verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

stories.note: John begins with the same words as Genesis: "In the beginning." "Dwelt among us" literally means "pitched his tent among us," like the tabernacle.
stories.draw: a single beam of golden light shining into deep darkness over the waters, echoing the first painting of Creation

stories.title: For God So Loved the World

verses.text: The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.

stories.note: John 3:16 may be the best-known verse in the Bible. Jesus spoke it to Nicodemus, a teacher of Israel who came to him by night.
stories.draw: the river Jordan at Bethany beyond Jordan at sunrise, reeds and still water, a lamb standing on the bank

stories.title: Never Thirst

verses.text: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.
And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.

stories.note: Jesus offered living water to a Samaritan woman, and called himself the bread of life after feeding five thousand. "I am the bread of life" is the first of his seven "I am" sayings in John.
stories.draw: an old stone well in Samaria at noon, a clay water jar left beside it, Mount Gerizim behind, a basket of five loaves and two fish on the grass nearby

stories.title: The Truth Shall Make You Free

verses.text: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

stories.note: At the Feast of Tabernacles great lamps were lit in the temple courts. In that setting Jesus said, "I am the light of the world."
stories.draw: the temple courts in Jerusalem at night during the Feast of Tabernacles, giant golden lampstands blazing, the city glowing below

stories.title: The Good Shepherd

verses.text: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:

stories.note: Shepherds in Israel often slept across the doorway of the fold. The Good Shepherd does more: he lays down his life for the sheep.
stories.draw: a stone sheepfold on a hillside at evening, sheep entering through the single gate, a shepherd seen from behind standing in the doorway

stories.title: The Resurrection and the Life

verses.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
Jesus wept.
And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.

stories.note: "Jesus wept" is the shortest verse in the KJV. He wept at the grave even though he was about to raise Lazarus from the dead.
stories.draw: a rock tomb at Bethany with its stone rolled away, light spilling out of the dark doorway, olive trees around

stories.title: The Way, the Truth, and the Life

verses.text: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me.
In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.
Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

stories.note: Jesus said these words at the Last Supper, the night before the cross. "Mansions" means dwelling places in the Father's house.
stories.draw: a lamp-lit stone house with many rooms on a hill, doors open and light pouring out onto a single path leading up to it

stories.title: That Ye Might Believe

verses.text: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.
Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.

stories.note: "It is finished" is one word in Greek, tetelestai, used for a debt paid in full. John tells us exactly why he wrote his Gospel: that we might believe.
stories.draw: the shore of the Sea of Galilee at dawn, a small charcoal fire with fish laid on it, a boat drawn up and nets full of fish

stories.title: Ye Shall Receive Power

verses.text: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
Which also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up into heaven? this same Jesus, which is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven.

stories.note: Acts 1:8 is an outline of the whole book: Jerusalem, Judaea and Samaria, then the ends of the earth. The angels promised he would return "in like manner."
stories.draw: the top of the Mount of Olives with a cloud of light rising into the sky, Jerusalem below, onlookers seen from behind

stories.title: Whosoever Shall Call

verses.text: And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.
And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.

stories.note: Pentecost, the Feast of Weeks, came fifty days after Passover. Peter preached from Joel 2, and about three thousand people believed that day.
stories.draw: an upper room at morning with a rushing wind blowing curtains, small flames of light hovering in the air, the city beyond the window

stories.title: The Road to Damascus

verses.text: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:
And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.

stories.note: Saul hunted Christians until the risen Christ met him on the road. Persecuting the church was persecuting Christ himself. Saul became Paul, who wrote thirteen New Testament letters.
stories.draw: a desert road near Damascus at noon, a blinding light bursting from the sky, a fallen traveller's cloak and staff in the dust

stories.title: They Searched the Scriptures

verses.text: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.

stories.note: The Bereans checked even an apostle's teaching against Scripture, and Luke calls them noble for it. Paul quoted Greek poets in Athens to meet his hearers where they were.
stories.draw: a synagogue room in Berea lit by oil lamps, scrolls unrolled on a long table, a window open to the evening

stories.title: Not Ashamed of the Gospel

verses.text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;

stories.note: Romans is Paul's fullest explanation of the gospel. Before the good news comes the bad news: no one measures up.
stories.draw: the city of Rome at dawn, seen from a hill, the road leading in and the river shining, a scroll letter sealed in the foreground

stories.title: The Gift of God

verses.text: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

stories.note: Wages are earned and a gift is received. God showed his love while we were still sinners, not after we improved.
stories.draw: a simple wrapped gift resting on a stone table in a ray of light, an open doorway behind leading out into a sunlit garden

stories.title: All Things Work Together

verses.text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

stories.note: Romans 8 begins with "no condemnation" and ends with "no separation." Nothing in all creation can separate us from God's love.
stories.draw: a wide river delta seen from above at sunset, many streams winding together into one great water flowing to the sea

stories.title: A Living Sacrifice

verses.text: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.

stories.note: After eleven chapters of what God has done, Paul writes "therefore." Living for God is the response to his mercy, not the way to earn it.
stories.draw: a stone altar in a quiet courtyard with a small fire, morning light, the city waking beyond the wall

stories.title: The Greatest of These

verses.text: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,
