For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.
And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.

stories.note: "Charity" in the KJV translates agape, self-giving love. A "glass" here is a polished metal mirror, which gave only a dim reflection.
stories.draw: an old bronze mirror on a table reflecting a soft blurred light from a window, three lit oil lamps beside it

stories.title: In the Twinkling of an Eye

verses.text: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?
But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

stories.note: 1 Corinthians 15 is the Bible's great resurrection chapter. Paul lists more than five hundred eyewitnesses of the risen Christ (15:6).
stories.draw: a vast sky at dawn with clouds parting and golden light streaming down over a quiet graveyard of old stones, trumpet-like rays of light

stories.title: A New Creature

verses.text: (For we walk by faith, not by sight:)
Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

stories.note: Paul asked three times for his "thorn in the flesh" to be removed. God's answer was not removal but grace.
stories.draw: a butterfly drying its wings on a twig beside an empty chrysalis, spring meadow behind in morning light

stories.title: The Fruit of the Spirit

verses.text: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.

stories.note: Paul says "fruit," not "fruits": one harvest with nine qualities, grown by the Spirit rather than manufactured by effort.
stories.draw: a vine and a fruit tree heavy with ripe fruit in a walled garden, grapes, figs and pomegranates in warm light

stories.title: By Grace Are Ye Saved

verses.text: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God:
Not of works, lest any man should boast.
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.

stories.note: Salvation is not by works, but it is for good works. "Workmanship" is the Greek poiema, the root of our word "poem."
stories.draw: a craftsman's workshop with a finished, beautiful carved piece on the bench, tools laid down, light from a high window

stories.title: The Whole Armour of God

verses.text: Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.
Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God:

stories.note: Paul wrote from prison, likely chained to a Roman soldier. The only weapon for attack in the armour is the sword of the Spirit, the word of God.
stories.draw: a Roman soldier's armour laid out on a wooden stand: helmet, shield, belt, breastplate and sword, in lamplight

stories.title: I Can Do All Things

verses.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

stories.note: Paul wrote "rejoice" again and again from prison. In context, "all things" means being content in plenty and in want (4:11-12).
stories.draw: a prison cell window with sunlight streaming in, a letter and quill on a small table, chains lying loose on the floor

stories.title: Set Your Affection on Things Above

verses.text: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.
Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men;

stories.note: Christ holds all things together. Because of that, ordinary work becomes service done "as to the Lord."
stories.draw: a hilltop above the clouds at dawn, the sky deep blue overhead with the morning star still shining

stories.title: Caught Up Together

verses.text: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.
In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

stories.note: Paul wrote this to comfort believers grieving those who had died: "Wherefore comfort one another with these words" (4:18).
stories.draw: a sky full of bright parting clouds over a sleeping town at dawn, rays of light streaming downward and upward

stories.title: Stand Fast

verses.text: Therefore, brethren, stand fast, and hold the traditions which ye have been taught, whether by word, or our epistle.
But the Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep you from evil.
But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing.

stories.note: The church in Thessalonica had been unsettled by false reports about the day of the Lord. Paul told them to stand fast in what they had been taught.
stories.draw: a lighthouse-like watchtower standing firm on a rocky coast as waves crash below, its lamp burning

stories.title: Godliness with Contentment

verses.text: For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;
Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
But godliness with contentment is great gain.

stories.note: Paul wrote to Timothy, a young pastor in Ephesus. "Conversation" in the KJV means way of life, not just speech.
stories.draw: a simple table with bread, a cup and an open scroll by a window, a quiet garden outside in soft light

stories.title: Rightly Dividing the Word

verses.text: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:

stories.note: 2 Timothy is Paul's last letter, written shortly before his death. "Inspiration of God" is literally "God-breathed."
stories.draw: a worn scroll and a carpenter's straightedge on a workbench, a lamp and a window looking out on a long road at sunset

stories.title: That Blessed Hope

verses.text: Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;
Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;

stories.note: Titus was left in Crete to set churches in order. Paul ties right living to looking forward to Christ's appearing.
stories.draw: the island of Crete at sunrise, cliffs over a sparkling sea, a small harbour town waking

stories.title: A Brother Beloved

verses.text: That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.
Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?

stories.note: Paul sent Onesimus, a runaway servant who had become a Christian, back to his master Philemon, asking that he be welcomed as a brother.
stories.draw: the open door of a house in Colossae at evening, a lamp in the window, a traveller's bag and staff set down at the threshold

stories.title: Quick and Powerful

verses.text: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.

stories.note: "Quick" in the KJV means living. God's word is alive and searches the heart, and Christ never changes.
stories.draw: a two-edged sword lying across an open scroll on a stone, a beam of light falling on both, deep shadows around

stories.title: Now Faith Is

verses.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

stories.note: Hebrews 11 is the hall of faith, from Abel to the prophets. Those witnesses surround us as we run our own race.
stories.draw: an ancient road leading toward a distant city of light on the horizon, tents and altars of travellers along the way, a starry dawn sky

stories.title: Doers of the Word

verses.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.

stories.note: James, the brother of the Lord, wrote a practical letter. Hearing without doing, he says, is like looking in a mirror and forgetting your own face (1:23-24).
stories.draw: a clear still pool reflecting a person's silhouette from behind, a path leading away from it into a busy village

stories.title: He Careth for You

verses.text: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

stories.note: Peter wrote to scattered believers facing hardship. "Peculiar" in the KJV means God's own special possession.
stories.draw: a fisherman's net and a heavy pack laid down on a lakeshore at sunset, the water calm and gold

stories.title: A Light That Shineth in a Dark Place

verses.text: We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:
But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

stories.note: Peter, an eyewitness of the transfiguration, still called the prophetic word "more sure," a lamp in a dark place. God's delay is patience, not slowness.
stories.draw: a lamp burning on a rock in a dark landscape just before dawn, the morning star bright above the horizon

stories.title: God Is Light

verses.text: This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

stories.note: John wrote so that believers could know they have eternal life (5:13). Forgiveness rests on God's faithfulness, not on how we feel.
stories.draw: sunlight breaking through a dark forest into a clearing, every shadow lit, a stream running clear

stories.title: God Is Love

verses.text: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.

stories.note: "God is love" appears only in 1 John 4 (verses 8 and 16). Our love is always a response; he loved first.
